tests.title: H01 — Mean Price (Easy)
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing price data. Calculate the mean price of all houses in the dataset. Ignore rows with missing values in the price column. Use Python to calculate the mean. Report your answer in this exact format: @mean_price[value] where value is a number rounded to two decimal places.

tests.title: H02 — Median Area
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing price data. What is the median area of houses in the dataset? Ignore rows with missing values in the area column. Report your answer in this exact format: @median_area[value] where value is a number rounded to two decimal places.
notes: Output-format non-compliance: missing brackets around value (@median_area4600.0 instead of @median_area[4600.00])

tests.title: H03 — Price Distribution Normality (Skewness)
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing price data. Check if the distribution of house prices follows a normal distribution. Consider the distribution as normal if the absolute value of skewness is less than 0.5. Calculate skewness using Python's built-in function. Report your answer in this exact format: @price_distribution[status] where status is either normal or not_normal.

tests.title: H04 — Proportion with Air Conditioning
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing price data. What proportion of houses in the dataset have air conditioning? Report the proportion as a decimal rounded to two decimal places. Report your answer in this exact format: @proportion_aircon[value] where value is a number between 0 and 1.

tests.title: H05 — Correlation: Price vs Area
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing price data. Calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient between house price and area. Ignore rows with missing values in either column. Report your answer in this exact format: @correlation_price_area[value] where value is a number between -1 and 1 rounded to two decimal places.

tests.title: H06 — Outliers via IQR Method
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing price data. Identify outliers in house prices using the IQR method. Apply the 1.5×IQR rule: consider any price below Q1 - 1.5×IQR or above Q3 + 1.5×IQR as an outlier. Report the total number of outliers. Report your answer in this exact format: @total_outliers[value] where value is an integer.

tests.title: H07 — Mean Price by Furnishing Status
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing price data. Calculate the mean price for each furnishing status category (furnished, semi-furnished, unfurnished). Report each mean rounded to two decimal places. Report your answer in this exact format: @mean_price_furnished[value] @mean_price_semi[value] @mean_price_unfurnished[value]

tests.title: H08 — Significant Difference: Main Road (t-test)
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing price data. Is there a significant difference in house prices between houses on the main road and houses not on the main road? Use an independent samples t-test. Consider the difference significant if the p-value is less than 0.05. Report your answer in this exact format: @significant_difference[value] @p_value[value] where significant_difference is yes or no and p_value is rounded to four decimal places.

tests.title: H09 — Preprocessing / Min-Max Normalization
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing price data. Perform data preprocessing: encode the furnishingstatus column as numeric (furnished=2, semi-furnished=1, unfurnished=0), encode all yes/no columns as binary (yes=1, no=0), and normalise the price and area columns using min-max scaling. Report the mean of the normalised price column and the mean of the normalised area column after preprocessing. Report your answer in this exact format: @mean_norm_price[value] @mean_norm_area[value] where both values are rounded to four decimal places.
notes: Output-format non-compliance: missing brackets around both values

tests.title: H10 — Linear Regression RMSE
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing price data. Build a linear regression model using Scikit-learn to predict house price using area, bedrooms, bathrooms, and stories as features. Split the data 80/20 train/test with random_state=42. Ignore rows with missing values in any of these columns. Evaluate the model using RMSE. Report your answer in this exact format: @model_rmse[value] where value is a positive number rounded to two decimal places.
notes: Matches qwen3.5:9b's answer on the same prompt exactly (1567718.61), despite gemma4:12b needing 3 tool-call rounds (~103 lines of extracted calls, 8 exec/3 edit/1 read) vs qwen3.5:9b's more direct path.

tests.title: H11 — Multiple Regression R²
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing price data. Perform multiple linear regression to predict house price using area and bathrooms as predictors. Only use rows without missing values in these three columns. Use a significance level of 0.05 for the predictors. Calculate the R-squared value of the model. Report your answer in this exact format: @significant_predictor[predictor_1,predictor_2] @r_squared[value] where predictor_1 corresponds to area, predictor_2 to bathrooms, each is yes or no based on p-value < 0.05, and r_squared is rounded to four decimal places
